instruction:
Compare the written open-content policies of the Cleveland Museum of Art, Smithsonian, Getty and National Gallery of Art. Use their open-access and linked policy/FAQ HTML, including https://www.si.edu/openaccess/faq, https://www.getty.edu/projects/open-content-program/faqs/ and https://www.nga.gov/terms-and-notices#open-access. Build four rows identifying the designation that establishes coverage, material covered, commercial reuse/modification wording, credit requirements versus recommendations, and other-rights limits. Assess six fictional proposals: a Cleveland image explicitly labelled CC0 used on commercial merchandise; a Smithsonian CC0 image cropped for a poster; Smithsonian content marked with a copyright restriction but no CC0 designation reused under an assumed blanket licence; a Getty Open Content image modified for sale without credit; an unmarked Getty website image treated as Open Content; and a National Gallery image excluded from open access treated as automatically reusable because it is visible online. State whether the cited policy establishes the proposed permission, what condition or qualification controls, and what cannot be concluded from it. Separate copyright permission from privacy, publicity, trademarks and endorsement where addressed. Cite each assessment and give three cross-institution distinctions. Review policy only; do not download, republish or request material.

Stopping condition: Stop when four policy rows, six evidence-backed case assessments and three distinctions are complete, with mandatory and recommended conditions kept separate.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Four policy rows covering the specified institutions
items.description: Output includes four distinct rows or sections analyzing the open-content policies of the Cleveland Museum of Art, Smithsonian, Getty, and National Gallery of Art. Full credit if all four are present. Partial credit if some are missing without explanation. Full credit for any missing row if the agent attempted to access that institution's site but encountered a block, error, or site-down issue and clearly reported the unavailability.

For each accessible institution, the row must identify the designation that establishes coverage, material covered, commercial reuse/modification wording, credit requirements versus recommendations, and other-rights limits (privacy, publicity, trademarks, endorsement). Full credit if all required details are addressed for the available institutions. Do not penalize for missing details if the respective institution's site was inaccessible or the policy text was removed, provided the limitation is reported. Assess other-rights qualifications only where the policy addresses them, including in the six case assessments; do not require unsupported claims. Cite the policy/FAQ source URLs supporting the rows and assessments.

Assess the fictional proposal of using a Cleveland image explicitly labelled CC0 on commercial merchandise. Full credit if it evaluates permission, controlling condition, what cannot be concluded, separates copyright from other rights, and includes citation. Full credit if the Cleveland policy is inaccessible or lacks sufficient detail due to site changes, and the agent reports this external limitation.

items.criterion: Assessment 2: Smithsonian CC0 cropped for poster
items.description: Assess the fictional proposal of using a Smithsonian CC0 image cropped for a poster. Full credit if it evaluates permission, controlling condition, what cannot be concluded, separates copyright from other rights, and includes citation. Full credit if the Smithsonian policy is inaccessible or lacks sufficient detail due to site changes, and the agent reports this external limitation.

items.criterion: Assessment 3: Smithsonian restricted content blanket license
items.description: Assess the fictional proposal of reusing Smithsonian content marked with a copyright restriction but no CC0 designation under an assumed blanket licence. Full credit if it evaluates permission, controlling condition, what cannot be concluded, separates copyright from other rights, and includes citation. Full credit if the Smithsonian policy is inaccessible or lacks sufficient detail due to site changes, and the agent reports this external limitation.

items.criterion: Assessment 4: Getty Open Content modified for sale without credit
items.description: Assess the fictional proposal of modifying a Getty Open Content image for sale without credit. Full credit if it evaluates permission, controlling condition, what cannot be concluded, separates copyright from other rights, and includes citation. Full credit if the Getty policy is inaccessible or lacks sufficient detail due to site changes, and the agent reports this external limitation.

items.criterion: Assessment 5: Unmarked Getty image as Open Content
items.description: Assess the fictional proposal of treating an unmarked Getty website image as Open Content. Full credit if it evaluates permission, controlling condition, what cannot be concluded, separates copyright from other rights, and includes citation. Full credit if the Getty policy is inaccessible or lacks sufficient detail due to site changes, and the agent reports this external limitation.

items.criterion: Assessment 6: NGA excluded image treated as reusable
items.description: Assess the fictional proposal of treating a National Gallery image excluded from open access as automatically reusable because it is visible online. Full credit if it evaluates permission, controlling condition, what cannot be concluded, separates copyright from other rights, and includes citation. Full credit if the NGA policy is inaccessible or lacks sufficient detail due to site changes, and the agent reports this external limitation.

Provide exactly three cross-institution distinctions based on their policies. Full credit for providing three valid distinctions based on accessible policies. Partial credit for fewer. Full credit if fewer distinctions are provided because fewer than two institution policies were successfully accessed due to external errors/blocks, and the agent explicitly noted this constraint.

items.criterion: Separation of mandatory and recommended conditions
items.description: Ensure that mandatory requirements (e.g., must credit) and recommended conditions (e.g., requested but not legally required to credit) are clearly distinguished throughout the output. Full credit if separation is consistently maintained for whatever policies the agent was able to access and review.
